hits.title: Call center quality assurance best practices: 2026 guide - Level AI
hits.snippet:
For organizations that review calls manually, QA specialists and managers may rely on certain call center metrics and KPIs — like average handle time (AHT) — to decide whether to select a call for review.

They often need to listen to an entire call to fully assess agent behavior, which can be time-consuming and limit the number of calls an analyst or manager can review daily. [...] How many calls should actually be scored for call center QA?

Traditional manual QA typically evaluates only about 2–5 calls per agent per week, which works out to roughly 1–2% of total volume. The common complaint is that this tiny sample isn't representative and lets both great and poor calls go unseen. The modern best practice is to use automated quality assurance software to score close to 100% of interactions, then route the flagged outliers to humans for deeper review. [...] A common complaint is that QA feels like a compliance exercise that doesn't change anything. SQM Group research found 83% of agents believe their QA program doesn't help them improve CSAT. QA only drives improvement when it's tied to frequent, personalized coaching with closed feedback loops, when agents help shape what's measured, and when trends from QA data feed directly into training and process changes rather than sitting in a monthly report.

hits.title: Quality Assurance in Call Centres: An Ultimate Guide
hits.snippet:
In call centres and contact centres, managers use QA to maintain consistent and high-quality customer service. This involves monitoring every interaction between agents and customers, to assess overall call quality, agent skills, and compliance.

The data gathered from customer service quality assurance helps you to measure performance against key metrics, and use it to improve not just customer experiences but also operational efficiency. [...] ## What is quality assurance (QA) in a call centre or contact centre?

Quality assurance (QA) is a process that ensures your products or services are meeting the standards you’ve put in place. Through continuous monitoring and evaluation, organisations can identify any problems or gaps in service and take necessary actions to improve. [...] It’s not just about customer experience, either. QA is good for employee motivation and engagement, too. Based on the data, you can offer extra training for agents who are struggling, and reward those who excel. This will help you to reduce staff turnover (and recruitment costs).

Finally, quality assurance brings operational benefits as it enables you to identify inefficiencies like poor scheduling and time-consuming manual tasks.

The main objectives of contact center quality assurance are to optimize overall agent performance, ensure compliance with company policies, and improve customer satisfaction.
